hook.text: Body is how coffee feels in your mouth—thin like tea, or thick like cream. It's a texture, not a flavor.

buildup.text: Oils and suspended solids create body. Metal filters let oils through; paper filters trap them.

discovery.text: French press coffee has heavy body because the metal mesh lets oils and fine particles into your cup.

twist.text: Espresso has the heaviest body of all—emulsified oils under pressure create a syrupy, coating texture.

climax.text: Brew method determines body more than bean choice. The same bean can feel thin or thick depending on method.

punchline.text: Flavor is what you taste. Body is what you feel. Both matter.

quiz.question: Why does French press coffee have more body than pour-over?
options: The metal mesh lets oils and particles through

details.summary: Body describes coffee's weight and texture in the mouth, from thin and watery to thick and syrupy. Oils, dissolved solids, and fine particles all contribute. Brew method heavily influences body: French press produces full body while paper-filtered coffee feels lighter and cleaner.
details.whyItMatters: Body is one of the key sensory dimensions of coffee. Matching body preference to brew method helps you make coffee you actually enjoy.
takeaways: Body ranges from thin and tea-like to thick and syrupy
Oils and suspended particles increase perceived body
Metal filters allow more oils through than paper filters

faq.question: Which brew method produces the heaviest body?
faq.answer: Turkish coffee has the heaviest body because ultra-fine grounds remain suspended. Espresso is also very full-bodied due to emulsified oils and high concentration. French press retains oils that paper filters would trap, producing medium-heavy body.

faq.question: Does roast level affect body?
faq.answer: Yes. Darker roasts generally produce heavier body because more oils migrate to the bean surface and dissolve during brewing. The cell structure breaks down further, releasing more soluble material. Light roasts tend to be lighter in body but more complex in acidity.
